fields.acceptance: A unit test of rhiza run milestone-check covers: no milestone served and no policy.toml passes; no milestone served with backlog = "skip" fails naming the change set; a run with a milestone whose change set serves it directly, or through an intent under it, passes; one serving another milestone or none fails naming it. A testscript runs a plan run with a fake agent (left live after rhiza session done) whose change set serves an intent under no milestone: it enters review with no policy.toml, and ends failed at milestone-check with backlog = "skip"
fields.statement: rhiza run milestone-check passes a planned change set that serves no milestone, and fails, naming it and the fix, only when the run was started with a milestone (request --milestone, RHIZA_MILESTONE) and the change set does not serve that milestone directly or through an intent under it, or when the repo's .rhiza/policy.toml [schedule] backlog is "skip" (with today's message, since that work would never be built)

fields.acceptance: internal/guide plan_test asserts the plan guide names RHIZA_MILESTONE, says a milestone is linked only when RHIZA_MILESTONE is set or one fits, names .rhiza/policy.toml's backlog rule and its "skip" exception, and no longer says every change set must serve a milestone; the installed skill copy matches the guide text
fields.statement: The plan guide (rhiza guide plan and the rhiza-plan skill) says an intention change set serves the intent it belongs under and links a milestone only when RHIZA_MILESTONE names one (then the serves link must reach it) or an open milestone fits; work no milestone fits is built as backlog by the repo's .rhiza/policy.toml [schedule] backlog rule, unless that rule is "skip", when it must serve a milestone as before
